text: The most hyped spot in GTA 6 is Vice City's beach, and it's copied from a real place, Miami's South Beach.
That glowing strip has about eight hundred old buildings from the nineteen twenties and thirties, many lit up with neon.
But a little over a hundred years ago, this beach didn't really exist.
It was a swamp full of tangled mangrove trees, with so many mosquitoes they turned people's white clothes black.
In nineteen thirteen, a rich man named Carl Fisher decided to build a city on it anyway.
Workers chopped down the mangroves by hand. Then giant machines sucked sand off the bottom of the bay and sprayed it over the swamp.
Six million cubic yards of sand. That's enough to fill about eighteen hundred Olympic pools.
He even had an elephant named Rosie helping out on the job.
And the ocean keeps washing it away, so on big repair jobs, trucks dump hundreds of loads of fresh sand a day.
So when you cruise Vice City's beach, you're driving on a copy of a beach that people built by hand.
